video_title: The Celtics Can't Buy a Bucket (Looking at You, Derrick White) | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Celtics' over-reliance on three-point shooting during recent slump
quotes.excerpt: you live by the three, you die by the three, and I think that's the philosophy
quotes.quote: It goes back to that age-old adage of you live by the three, you die by the three, and I think that's the philosophy for the Boston Celtics. You look at the past two games, they've only lost their last two games by a total of two points. Of course, you want to win in Denver; Denver has been playing at a high, high level. And then you caught a hot Magic team; Franz Wagner, he's playing unbelievable. But I think one thing that occurs is you pay attention to their defensive rating, and they're still doing enough to stop guys. They're still doing enough to win, but it's all about, do you want to be more versatile offensively?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Celtics need to prioritize scoring inside over shooting threes
quotes.excerpt: The end of last season, what was the topic of conversation around Boston? How can we put more pressure on the rim.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The end of last season, what was the topic of conversation around Boston? How can we put more pressure on the rim. That's why they were in the Jayson Tatum to DeAndre Ayton sweepstakes. Brad Stevens did some media availability towards the end of the season, said he doesn't hate the number of threes, but he acknowledges you got to put more pressure on the rim.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White's declining shooting performance is a major concern
quotes.excerpt: Derrick White's shooting is not a short-term thing. He's shooting less than 30% from the field.
quotes.quote: I am concerned, though, about Derrick White. Derrick White's shooting is not a short-term thing. He's shooting less than 30% from the field, and he has been in steady decline over the last year and a half. That's concerning to me. I think Payton Pritchard will figure it out, and they need him to figure it out because he is a shot creator for that team. But Derrick White's shooting numbers, that is a real problem for this team because as good as he is defensively and as solid as he is as a playmaker, he's got to make open shots.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White's confidence and role in the Celtics' offense
quotes.excerpt: I think his confidence has been affected. He had at least two or three seconds to drive that ball
quotes.quote: I think his confidence has been affected. You look at the Sacramento game, he had at least two or three seconds to drive that ball, attack, and try to make a play. I just feel as though ever since last season, he's been trying to find his shot and kind of been inside his head. But it's so necessary because, like we said prior, you can't rely on a 36, 37-year-old Paul George to be shooting and playing out of his mind, averaging mid-20s. He's been a great three-and-D guy, he'll be a great third option, but I think Derrick White definitely has to step up in order for this team to be anything, space the floor, but at the same time, take pressure off Jayson Tatum and even Payton Pritchard.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Opposing teams are successfully forcing Jayson Tatum into turnovers
quotes.excerpt: Teams are going to continue to do this to Tatum. They're going to continue to pressure him
quotes.quote: Teams are going to continue to do this to Tatum. They're going to continue to pressure him, to blitz him, to send double teams at him. And if you look at some of the numbers, it's having an effect. His first 12 games, Tatum averaged 7.3 assists per game. Last three, he's down to 4.3. Turnovers, first 12 games, 2.7. Last three, five. Assist-to-turnover ratio, obviously, not as good: 2.7 the first 12 games, less than one, 0.86 over the last three. Teams are just going to try everything they can to take the ball out of Tatum's hands.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Celtics miss a second dominant scoring option to alleviate pressure
quotes.excerpt: you miss a second dominant option. It's not being negative, it's not saying, oh, we wish we still had this
quotes.quote: It's these moments, not bringing it up, but you miss a second dominant option. It's not being negative, it's not saying, oh, we wish we still had this, but it's like, yo, there's moments where you miss the guy that's attacking in the mid-range. You miss the guy that's just making you pay for even trapping your man. I believe they'll find it, but just got to step up with making those threes. I believe they'll figure it out in the long run, but you definitely won't be winning many good nights without, you know, Paul George playing at a high, high level.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner's confidence in Paul George and Payton Pritchard
quotes.excerpt: I'm more confident in Paul George stepping up and being that second option
quotes.quote: I'm more confident in Paul George stepping up and being that second option and Payton Pritchard having the ball off the bench and be 20 per night in big games. I feel as though historically, Derrick White has always made his living being at third or fourth option or kind of hiding in the open. It's different from being like, hey, you're going to get some of Drew Holiday's shots or some of Drew Holiday's opportunities, and we mix it in when you have one of the best, highest-paid teams in NBA history, to now it's going to be like, yo, Jayson is out, you're going to have to be the second option whether you think so or not.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White's shooting decline from championship season to present
quotes.excerpt: Derrick White's shooting is a concern for me. It's a real concern for me with this shooting.
quotes.quote: I mentioned the decline of Derrick White to keep it focused on him for a second. 23-24, the year the Celtics won the championship, he shot 46% from the field, close to 40% from three. That was like a high-water mark for Derrick White. That's when it's like, all right, this guy is the best third or fourth option in the NBA. The following season, 44%, 38%. Still good, still good numbers. Last season, 39.4% from the field, 32.7% from three. This year, so far, 41% from the field, 28.9% from three. So this has basically been a steady decline for four years now. That's it's just a concern for me. It's a real concern for me with this shooting.
